caption:
Watched someone spend 4 hours designing a carousel in Canva yesterday.

Custom graphics. Perfect color matching. Smooth animations. Posted it.

147 likes. Average swipe-through probably 2 slides.

Why? Because they started with design. Not flow.

The structure was: 

Slide 1 hook → Slide 2-9 random tips → Slide 10 CTA. 

No tension. No curiosity thread. No reason to keep swiping after slide 3.

Pretty can’t save broken flow.

Our process: Claude builds skeleton first (hook testing, tension structure, curiosity gaps, value progression). 

Refines copy (removes generic, adds personality, checks momentum). Then Canva translates structure to visuals (hierarchy, rhythm, variety).

Strategy → structure → design. In that order.

Completion rate is what triggers distribution. Not how nice slide 5 looks.

title: Claude + Canva Workflow for Viral Carousels
one_liner: Use Claude to build narrative structure first, then design in Canva for high-completion carousels.
key_points: Beautiful design flops without flow — weak hooks and no tension cause users to stop swiping by slide 3
Start in Claude: generate scroll-stopping hooks, contrarian angles, and a 10-slide tension-to-CTA structure
Each slide must build momentum toward the next, not just contain information
Design in Canva last — strategy → structure → design is the order that drives completion rates
